chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' until he returned to his family. He said: 'He should send [someone] to perform Tawaf on his behalf. If he dies before Tawaf is performed for him, his Wali (guardian) should perform Tawaf on his behalf.'
And that which indicates that it is only permissible for him to command another to perform Tawaf on his behalf when it is difficult for him and he is unable to do it himself is what he narrated.

key_terms.طَوَافَ اَلنِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed by men to complete Hajj
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: His Wali (guardian/heir), who performs the ritual on behalf of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' and returns home or dies?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *Tawaf al-Nisa'* (Farewell Circumambulation) for those who depart Mecca before its completion, emphasizing the permissibility of proxy performance (*niyabah*) when physical presence is no longer possible. The text distinguishes between the general delegation to any representative and the specific obligation on the heir (*Wali*) if death occurs, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that acts of worship can be fulfilled by others when the original actor is incapacitated or absent. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Hajj rituals to ensure the pilgrim’s obligations are met even in cases of forgetfulness or death.
